<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par47" />{{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹל}} is found in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, in every case after the regular form; but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=14}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=10}}, where the 2nd fem. precedes and follows, probably {{GHGheb|text=תִּזְרָעִין וּב׳}} is to be read with Marti for {{GHGheb|text=תִּזְרָעֶ֫נּוּ}}.—For the ''3rd plur. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנַה}} we find in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=11}}, in pause {{GHGheb|text=תִּבְטָ֫חוּ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תִּבְטַ֫חְנָה}}), and thrice (as if to distinguish it from the 2nd pers.) the form {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטֹ֫לְנָה}} with the preformative {{GHGheb|text=י}} (as always in Western Aram., Arab, Eth., and Assyr.), in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=22}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנָה}} appears in some cases to be incorrectly used even for the fem. of the 3rd pers. or for the masc. of the 2nd pers. ''sing.'' as {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁלַ֫חְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=26}} (where, however, perhaps {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁלָחֶ֫נָּה}} is to be read), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=13}}, for 2nd sing. masc., according to Olshausen a corruption of {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁלַח יָד}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=3|hidebook=1}} for {{GHGheb|text=תָּרֹ֫נָּה}} read {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְנֶה}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=23}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=10}} read {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְרָאֵ֫נוּ}} with the Samaritan.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, as also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=16}} (if we read {{GHGheb|text=טֽוֹבָתִי}} with LXX for the 2nd {{GHGheb|text=תקותי}}), it is equally possible to explain the form as a plural. This small number of examples hardly justifies our finding in the above-mentioned passages the remains of an emphatic form of the Impf., analogous to the Arab. ''Modus energicus I'', with the termination ''ănnă''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|l}}
For {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} we frequently find, especially in the Pentateuch and mostly after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, simply {{GHGheb|text=ןָ|pron=nā}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=33.36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=18.19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=55|hidebook=1}}; in Arab. always ''nă''. According to Elias Levita {{GHGheb|text=תִּלְבַּ֫שְׁןָ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=18}}) is the only example of this kind in the strong verb. The form {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּגְּבְּהֶ֫ינָה}} (so also Qimḥi and ed. Mant.; but Baer, Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּגְּבְּהֶ֫נָה}}) for {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּגְבַּ֫הְנָה|translate=they were high}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=50}}, is irregular, with {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}} inserted after the manner of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGpar|67|d}}; {{GHGpar|72|i}}; according to Olshausen it is an error caused by the following form.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|m}}
'''4.''' Instead of the plural forms in {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} there are, especially in the older books, over 300 forms<ref>[See details in F. Böttcher, ''Lehrb.'', § 930; and cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=15}}.]</ref> with the fuller ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} (with ''Nûn paragogicum''), always bearing the tone; cf. {{GHGpar|29|m}} and {{GHGpar|44|l}}; on its retention before suffixes, see {{GHGpar|60|e}}; also defectively {{GHGheb|text=יְרִיבֻן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, &c. This usually expresses marked emphasis, and consequently occurs most commonly at the end of sentences (in the principal pause), in which case also the (pausal) vowel of the second syllable is generally retained. Thus there arise full-sounding forms such as {{GHGheb|text=יִלְקֹט֑וּן|translate=they collect}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִרְגָּז֑וּן|translate=they tremble}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁמָע֑וּן|translate=ye shall hear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=17}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=13}}, with Zaqeph qaṭon, Athnaḥ, and Silluq; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=15}}, with Segolta; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=8}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=13|hidebook=1}} with Zaqeph qaṭon, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=12|hidebook=1}} with Athnaḥ and Silluq, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=5|hidebook=1}} after {{GHGterm|wāw consec}}. Without the pause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=11|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=יִדְרְכוּן קֶ֫שֶׁת}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=4|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=28.29.30}} ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁאָלוּן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=9}} ({{GHGheb|text=יִקְצֹרוּן}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁאֲבוּן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=18}} after {{GHGterm|wāw consec}}.

Some of these examples may be partly due to euphonic reasons, e.g. certainly {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=6}}, and often, to avoid a hiatus before {{GHGheb|text=א}} or {{GHGheb|text=ע}}. It was, however, the pause especially which exerted an influence on the restoration of this older and fuller termination (cf. {{GHGpar|159|c}}, note), as is manifest from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=11}}: {{GHGheb|text=בַּל־יְֽחֱזָי֑וּן יֶֽחֱזוּ וְיֵב֫שׁוּ}} ''they see not; may they see and become''<section end="par47" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
